_comment: Hand-authored manifest and the only input of the kabic pipeline. Each `domains` entry drives extraction to ke_api.json and the C#, C and Zig backends (kabic generate); each `bindings` entry configures ClangSharp (kabic bindings). Adding a domain here is what migrating it to kabic means mechanically. Never a derived artifact.

domains._comment: The scheduler contract. register_system's params carry queries + access_list, which the wave builder orders on; a hand-written IRuntime had omitted them, so every C#-registered system declared zero access and the wave builder saw zero conflicts. Generating the surface from the header is what keeps that from drifting again. system_ctx.h rides along because the execute callback's first parameter is a ke_system_ctx*.
domains.name: runtime

domains._comment: The physics domain's node surface. Node3D (spatial) and the body enums/handles physics_2d.h owns arrive via composeHeaders: this domain describes only the components, while the domains owning those types keep emitting them.
domains.name: physics_components

domains._comment: Audio's node surface. AudioPlayer used to exist only as a hand-written C# class reading an untyped property bag, so no other language could be one and no field had a type or a default; describing it here is what makes it a node in every language at once. Node3D arrives via composeHeaders, same as render_components.
domains.name: audio_components

domains._comment: auxHeaders are included purely so ke_render_service's own typedef'd primitives (ke_gpu_buffer et al.) and enum params (ke_alpha_mode) resolve to real C# types instead of an unresolvable bare name; only their TypedefDecls are extracted (see extract_api.cs --aux), so their own vtables/enums/functions never get described or re-emitted here, avoiding both noise and a duplicate/shadowing definition of bindings ClangSharp already generated elsewhere under their own literal names.
domains.name: render

domains._comment: The data a loader answers with, described where it is declared rather than in one plugin's binding project, so every plugin answering with it reads one projection instead of one per binding.
domains.name: mesh_data

domains._comment: auxHeaders (same reason as render's) resolve ke_render_service's own cross-domain typedefs; the resolve_*_into slots' `core` param is tagged [opaque] so the generated method takes void* (matching the ClangSharp-generated ke_asset_resolver delegate field, which itself collapses ke_render_service* to void* since Framework never sees a concrete render backend's own struct).
domains.name: asset_resolver

domains._comment: node3d.h: transform.h is [node:]-tagged (whole-struct mode — see CSharpWriter's [whole:] tag) to generate Node3D itself into Framework, not a domain-specific project, since every other assembly's node types (Render.Webgpu, Physics, Audio) inherit it.
domains.name: spatial

domains._comment: The signal bus. Emission is a frame's event, connection is durable data; the vtable is what lets a node in any language be either end of a wire.
domains.name: signal_bus

domains._comment: The entity-to-script binding. Every scripting runtime otherwise keeps this map itself, which is what makes a node authored in one language invisible to another.
domains.name: script_host

domains._comment: Not a separate native plugin — components.h lives inside src/c/render (no build.zig, no .so of its own), same as world/scene_tree/scene_loader/input_actions below are four manifest entries under one native 'framework' plugin. This entry is render's node-ergonomics header: a plain [node:]-tagged struct emits a node type (Camera/DirectionalLight/PointLight/SpotLight/AmbientLight). outDir points into render's own C# project: there is no 'toolkit' project — every domain hosts its own node types, physically, in its own project (this one for render's; physics/audio host their own node types the same way).
domains.name: render_components

domains._comment: render/ui/components.h is the UI overlay pass's component vocabulary, split out of the plugin's own ui_create.h so the node surface (Label) generates from a contract header the same way render_components does — the factory header keeps only the vtable it creates.
domains.name: ui_components
